body: Ind AS 7/IAS 7 lets interest paid sit in operating OR financing, and interest/dividends received in operating OR investing; US ASC 230 forces operating. Ind AS 116 puts lease principal (and usually interest) in financing; US operating-lease cash stays in CFO. Acquisitions are investing everywhere, so serial acquirers show clean CFO and weak FCF-after-M&A. IFRS 18 (effective 2027 for IFRS reporters) removes the choice for most corporates (interest paid -> financing); India had not notified an Ind AS equivalent as of Nov-2026 - recheck before FY28. Lending subsidiaries: for an NBFC, loan growth is operating cash. Worked example L&T consolidated (Screener, Rs cr): PAT 4,966/4,592/6,486/8,004/10,217 in FY15-19 while CFO was -1,365/-3,240/6,655/-10,031/-4,756, largely the L&T Finance loan book; once it stopped growing CFO turned 23,074 (FY21), 22,777 (FY23). Lesson: for conglomerates use segment/standalone cash flow or strip the financing arm; restate Indian CFO to US basis by moving interest and lease payments back into it.
title: Cash-flow classification games: interest, leases, acquisitions, lending subsidiaries (L&T example)

body: Utkarsh SFB FY26: GNPA additions Rs 1,724 cr; reductions Rs 2,119 cr = write-offs 1,089 + ARC sale 654 + upgrades/recoveries only 375. ARC sale FY26: Rs 1,515 cr principal (428,864 accounts) for Rs 207 cr consideration (13.6%), SRs fully provided. GNPA % fell 12.4% -> 5.9% (Sep-25 -> Sep-26) mostly by removal, not cure. Same trap as Federal Bank (v1.3 protocol). Use net slippage (additions - upgrades - recoveries) per quarter and the write-off pool recovery rate as the asset-quality KPI.
title: Microfinance lenders 'cure' GNPA by write-offs and ARC sales at ~14 paise on the rupee: rebuild the NPA walk before believing an asset-quality turn
